— AI strategy

Find the useful role for AI in your business.

AI is most useful when it solves a specific problem. I help businesses assess where it can save effort, where it needs human oversight, and where a simpler process may be a better choice.

Discuss ai strategy

A connected approach to ai strategy

A practical AI strategy starts with tasks, information, and responsibilities. Drafting an internal outline is different from sending advice to a customer or handling confidential business data. Each use case needs an appropriate level of review, a clear owner, and a way to judge whether it improves the existing process. Buying tools before understanding those requirements often creates another disconnected system to maintain.

When this work can help

  • Teams are trying AI tools without shared guidance or data boundaries.
  • Repetitive marketing tasks consume time but lack a reliable workflow.
  • There is pressure to adopt AI without a clear business case.

How I approach the work

I map a small number of candidate tasks, review the data involved, and assess effort, cost, error risk, and the need for approval. We select a contained pilot with a manual fallback and a named owner. The pilot is evaluated against the current process before expanding access or automation. This creates evidence for a decision instead of assuming that every task benefits from AI.

Core activities & deliverables

Readiness and use cases

Review existing workflows, data quality, tool access, and team skills. Identify manageable tasks and exclude uses that require expertise or safeguards the business does not have.

Workflow design

Define inputs, templates, review steps, permissions, and failure handling. Keep human approval where output affects customers, spending, or important business records.

Evaluation and guidance

Agree a small evaluation set, record errors and revision time, and compare total cost. Create practical operating guidance for permitted use, verification, and escalation.

Who this is for

This work suits smaller businesses and marketing teams seeking controlled, useful adoption rather than an enterprise AI transformation. Examples include content research assistance, internal knowledge organization, draft preparation, and routine reporting support. Any integration depends on the tools, permissions, and data available; a pilot can remain manual when that is the more reliable choice.

What to consider before starting

AI can produce plausible but incorrect output, expose information through inappropriate use, and change behavior as models or products update. Human review remains necessary. I do not guarantee automated business outcomes, legal compliance, or visibility in AI search answers. Regulated advice, sensitive decisions, and confidential data may require specialist review or may be unsuitable for the proposed tools.

How we assess progress

A useful evaluation compares task completion time, review effort, error types, output usefulness, and ongoing tool cost. Savings should include the time spent correcting and maintaining the process. A workflow that produces more material without improving decisions or quality is not automatically a success.

Questions about ai strategy

Can AI replace our marketing team?+

My focus is on supporting specific tasks and improving workflows. Strategy, accountability, factual review, and understanding your customers still require people.

Will this help us appear in AI search?+

Clear, accessible, well-supported web content can help people and discovery systems understand your business. No consultant can guarantee inclusion or citations in AI-generated answers.
